T: Make it home to Coney before the dogs go cold.
D: A Coney Island gang fights its way home across New York after being framed for murder.
P: Serve the dogs when the gangs all gather in the park for the big meeting.
S: Warm soft pretzel bites brushed with butter and coarse salt, with a hot cheddar sauce and yellow mustard for dipping.

Mix 250g plain flour, 4g instant yeast, 1 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp salt and 160ml warm water. Knead 8 minutes, cover and rise 1 hour. Roll into ropes and cut into 24 bites. Simmer 1 litre water with 30g bicarbonate of soda; boil bites in batches for 20 seconds, drain and bake on baking paper at 220°C for 12 to 15 minutes. Brush with 20g melted butter. For dip, melt 15g butter, stir in 15g flour, whisk in 150ml milk and simmer 2 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in 100g grated cheddar. Serve with mustard.
Corn ribs roasted until charred and curling, brushed with chilli butter and smoked salt, finished with plenty of lime.

Quarter 4 corn cobs lengthways on a secure board with a sturdy sharp knife; use whole cobs if easier. Brush with 30g melted butter mixed with 1/2 tsp chilli flakes and a pinch of smoked salt. Roast at 220°C for 20 to 25 minutes, turning once, until tender and charred at the edges. Finish with the juice of 1 lime.
M: griddled frankfurts under loose spiced beef sauce, mustard and onion, can you dig it
Chilli sauce: fine beef mince stirred into water so it stays loose, onion, chilli powder, cumin, paprika and tomato paste, simmered 45 minutes. Over griddled franks with mustard and raw onion.
W: Vanilla ice cream, chewy chocolate cookies and dark chocolate.

Soften 500ml vanilla ice cream just enough to scoop. Sandwich between 8 large chewy chocolate cookies to make 4 sandwiches. Freeze on a lined tray for 1 hour. Melt 150g dark chocolate gently, cool until just warm, dip half of each sandwich and return to the freezer for 15 minutes. Make ahead so they're ready when the film finishes.
K: Ice-cold cola, cherry syrup and a squeeze of lime.
Fill 4 glasses with ice. Add 15ml cherry syrup to each, top each with 250ml cola and squeeze in a lime wedge. Stir once. Taste before adding more syrup.

steps.text: Mix the flour (keeping a spoonful back for the cheese dip), yeast, sugar, salt and warm water, then knead until smooth.
Cover and rise until doubled.
Roll into ropes and cut into 24 bites. Bring the boiling water and bicarbonate of soda to a simmer.
Boil the bites in batches for 20 seconds, then drain on baking paper.
Bake at 220C until deep golden, then brush with melted butter and coarse salt.
For the dip, melt butter, stir in the remaining flour, whisk in the milk and simmer. Off the heat, stir in the cheddar and serve with mustard.
Quarter the cobs lengthways on a secure board with a sturdy sharp knife (use whole cobs if easier). Melt the butter with the chilli flakes and smoked salt.
Brush the corn with the chilli butter.
Roast at 220C, turning once, until tender and charred at the edges. Finish with lime juice.
Dice the onion and keep a quarter aside for topping. Mince the garlic.
Fry the rest of the onion in the oil with the garlic, then add the mince and brown well.
Stir in the tomato paste, cumin, smoked paprika, tomatoes and water and simmer. Season with salt.
Bake the fries as directed on the packet.
Griddle the franks until piping hot and warm the buns. Fill with franks and chilli and finish with onion and mustard.

m.note: griddled frankfurts under loose spiced beef sauce, mustard and onion, can you dig it
m.how: Dice 1 onion; reserve a quarter for topping. Fry the rest in 1 tbsp oil with 2 minced garlic cloves, add 400g beef mince and brown well. Stir in 1 tbsp tomato paste, 1 tsp each ground cumin and smoked paprika, 400g tinned tomatoes and 100ml water. Simmer 25 minutes; season with salt. Bake 600g shoestring fries as directed on the packet. Griddle 8 beef franks until piping hot and warm 8 buns. Fill buns with franks and chilli; finish with reserved onion and mustard. Serve fries alongside.
